findings.title: Caching tests removed while caching logic remains in service
findings.body: The 'Caching' describe block (which previously verified that getAuthorizationConditions() and getFilterConditions() returned the same value on repeated calls) was removed entirely from the test file. The service still contains the caching implementation in lines 84-87 and 91-94 (`this.cachedAuthConditions` / `this.cachedFilterConditions` cache fields and the `if (this.cachedAuthConditions === undefined)` checks). Removing these tests is a regression in coverage: future refactors that silently break caching (e.g. accidentally re-fetching memberships on every call, losing the deduplication of identical `Prisma.sql` template-literal objects) would no longer be caught. The PR description also does not mention deleting caching tests, which can mislead reviewers.

findings.title: Public findMany method removed, breaking any external consumers
findings.body: The previous public API of `InsightsBookingService` was `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)`. This method has been deleted and replaced with `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>`, which returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment that callers must now embed in their own `prisma.$queryRaw` call. This is a breaking change to the service contract. The PR description does not mention updating other callers (e.g. insights API handlers or other modules that import this service). Before merging, every existing caller of `service.findMany(...)` must be migrated to use `getBaseConditions` + `$queryRaw`, otherwise the build will fail or runtime behavior will change.

findings.title: Test redefines NOTHING_CONDITION independently from the service
findings.body: The test file declares its own `const NOTHING_CONDITION = Prisma.sql`1=0`` (line 10) instead of importing the value from `insightsBooking.ts`, which keeps its own private copy of the same constant. If the service ever changes the definition of `NOTHING_CONDITION` (for example to `Prisma.sql`FALSE`` or some other falsy SQL expression), the assertions `expect(conditions).toEqual(NOTHING_CONDITION)` in this test file would still pass against the local copy, masking the regression. The service should export `NOTHING_CONDITION` and the tests should import it so both sides of the comparison are guaranteed to refer to the same value.
